chunks: he who makes it possible for his adversary to so overpower him as to remove the flesh (from his bones), crush his bones and cut his skin into pieces, then it means that his helplessness is great and his heart surrounded within the sides of his chest is weak. You may become like this if you wish,
But for me, before I allow it I shall use my sharp edged swords of al-Mashrafiyyah which would cut as under the bones of the head and fly away arms and feet.
Thereafter, Allah will do whatever He wills.

key_terms.الْمَشْرَفِيَّةُ: a type of sword, symbolizing decisive power
key_terms.جَوَانِحُ: sides of the chest (metaphor for the heart)
key_terms.فَرَاشُ الْهَامِ: the offspring of insects/creatures (metaphor for small remnants or fine cuts)
key_terms.يَعْرُقُ: to strip or remove flesh from bones

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean by 'Mashrafiyyah' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) contrasts the passive weakness of those who allow their enemies to dominate them with his own decisive military prowess, using the metaphor of the 'Mashrafiyyah' sword to illustrate his power to sever limbs and defeat foes. He asserts that while weakness leads to being consumed by enemies, his strength ensures victory, leaving the final outcome to God's will. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'Qudrah' (capability) and active resistance against oppression, distinguishing the righteous leader from the complacent.
